curriculum.lesson_evidence: Writing a poem from experience starts with a precise moment, builds an image bank of sensory details, then selects only the strongest images. A title can frame interpretation without explaining everything.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Build a six-item image bank for one real moment and circle the three you would keep.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Sensory and specific; selection justified by intensity or relevance.

CHECK
Writing a life summary instead of a moment. Poems often zoom in.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draft an original experience poem (12–20 lines) with a purposeful title and a note listing cut images.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

teach_steps.explain:
Writing a poem from experience starts with a precise moment, builds an image bank of sensory details, then selects only the strongest images. A title can frame interpretation without explaining everything.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked.
